learning_objective: 🕊️ Discover how theatre uses objects, colors, and actions as powerful symbols to communicate deep, unspoken messages to the audience!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: प्रतीक (एक वस्तु या क्रिया जो किसी गहरे विचार को दर्शाती है)
रूपक (किसी एक चीज़ का उपयोग दूसरी चीज़ को समझाने के लिए करना)
मूल भाव (नाटक में बार-बार दोहराया जाने वाला कोई विचार या चित्र)
निहितार्थ (संवाद के पीछे का छिपा हुआ असली अर्थ)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: On stage, a physical object often represents a larger idea. A withered tree might symbolize dying hope, a crown represents power, and a broken mirror might symbolize a shattered identity.

What a character wears tells a story. A villain wearing sharp, dark clothes or a hero dressed in bright, flowing fabrics uses color and texture to instantly communicate their personality without speaking a word.

Subtext is what characters are actually thinking while they say something else. An actor might say 'I'm fine' while aggressively scrubbing a plate—the action (scrubbing) is a symbol of their hidden anger.
Sounds can also be symbols. A slow, ticking clock playing in the background might symbolize the anxiety of waiting or the fact that a character's time is running out.

Modern theatre often uses minimalist sets where a simple wooden block can be a throne, a bed, or a mountain. This forces the audience to use their imagination and focus on the symbolic meaning of the space.

fun_activity.title: 🌂 The Magic Umbrella
fun_activity.instructions: Take an umbrella. In 60 seconds, act out three different scenes where the umbrella is NOT an umbrella. Use it as a sword, a walking stick for an old man, and a guitar. This is how actors use symbolic imagination!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly define the difference between a simple Prop (used for its actual purpose) and a Symbol (used to represent an abstract idea).
📌 Be ready to give an example of how color psychology works in costume design (e.g., Red for passion/danger, White for purity).
📌 Explain the concept of 'Subtext' as the 'hidden river of emotion' running underneath the spoken dialogue.
quick_recap: ⭐ A motif is a recurring symbol that helps build the central theme of the play.
⭐ Lighting can act as a metaphor (e.g., a harsh spotlight for interrogation, soft blue for loneliness).
⭐ Symbolic theatre relies heavily on the audience's active participation to decode the meanings.
